memory_candidates.content: When deleting a command/skill/agent file from the agent-system source store, check-extension-docs.sh's Rule K (deployed-command-orphan detection) can NEVER fire for the deployed .claude/ tree, because .claude/ is entirely gitignored and Rule K's check_flat_category_orphans() enumerates deployed files via `git -C "$REPO_ROOT" ls-files "<category>"`, which returns nothing for any gitignored path. Do not expect (or wait for) a Rule K FAIL/PASS transition as evidence that stale deployed copies were pruned -- verify with a direct `ls` of the deployed directory instead. This applies to any deployed category (commands, agents, scripts) under a gitignored deploy root.

When a task's plan explicitly names literal deleted-file paths as required verification text (e.g. 'zero grep hits for path X anywhere under scripts/'), retargeted explanatory comments describing what used to call a now-deleted file must avoid spelling out the literal deleted path -- describe it generically ('the three former lifecycle command files') instead. A first-draft retarget that names the old path for historical context will fail the plan's own grep-based verification.
